indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.5.1.2 Identify, discuss and appreciate the natural and human features of the environment and the need to keep the environment clean
indicator.objective: Know how to keep washrooms clean

skills.description: Explain why washrooms should be kept clean (prevents germs, bad smell, disease).
Identify ways to keep washrooms clean (flush after use, aim properly, dispose of tissue in bins, regular cleaning).
State what can happen if washrooms are not kept clean (bad smell, flies, spread of disease).
Describe proper behaviour in a washroom (e.g. flushing, washing hands after use).
Design a poster to encourage clean washroom habits.
Explain how learners can help keep school washrooms clean.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Washrooms are only for adults to keep clean.
Throwing tissue on the floor is acceptable.
A dirty washroom only smells bad, but is not a health risk.
Washrooms do not need to be cleaned regularly.
Hand washing after using the washroom is not necessary.

questions.stem: Why should washrooms be kept clean?
options: To prevent germs and bad smell
hints: Dirty washrooms can smell and have germs.
questions.explanation: Washrooms should be kept clean to prevent germs, bad smell and the spread of disease.

questions.stem: Which of these is a reason for keeping washrooms clean?
options: To stop the spread of diseases
hints: Germs can spread in dirty washrooms.
questions.explanation: Keeping washrooms clean helps stop the spread of diseases.
questions.misconception: A dirty washroom is only a smell problem.

questions.stem: Give one reason why washrooms should be kept clean.
questions.explanation: Washrooms should be kept clean to prevent germs, bad smell and disease.

questions.stem: A dirty washroom can attract flies. Why is this a health risk?
options: Flies can carry germs from the washroom to food and people
Flies make the washroom look pretty
Flies make the washroom smell better
hints: They can carry germs to food.
questions.explanation: Flies attracted to dirty washrooms can carry germs to food and people, spreading disease.

questions.stem: What should you do immediately after using a toilet?
questions.explanation: You should flush the toilet immediately after use to keep it clean and prevent bad smell.

questions.stem: Where should used tissue paper be placed?
hints: It should go into a bin.
questions.explanation: Used tissue paper should be placed in a waste bin to keep the washroom clean.
questions.misconception: Throwing tissue on the floor is acceptable.

questions.stem: State one way to keep a washroom clean.
hints: Think about what you do after using the toilet.
questions.explanation: Ways to keep washrooms clean include flushing after use, putting tissue in the bin, and cleaning regularly.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a good way to keep a washroom clean?
hints: Which action makes the washroom dirty?
Tissue on the floor is not clean.
questions.explanation: Throwing tissue on the floor makes the washroom dirty. The other actions help keep it clean.
questions.misconception: Throwing tissue on the floor is acceptable.

questions.stem: What can happen if a washroom is not kept clean?
options: It can smell bad and spread diseases
questions.explanation: A dirty washroom can smell bad and spread diseases.
questions.misconception: A dirty washroom is only a smell problem.

questions.stem: State one consequence of not keeping a washroom clean.
questions.explanation: Not keeping a washroom clean can cause bad smell, flies and the spread of disease.

questions.stem: A school washroom is not cleaned for many days. What is the most likely health effect on learners?
options: Learners may get sick from germs
hints: Germs build up in dirty places.
questions.explanation: If a washroom is not cleaned for many days, germs build up and learners may get sick.
questions.misconception: Dirty washrooms do not affect health.

questions.stem: What should you do after using a washroom?
options: Wash your hands with soap and water
Wipe your hands on your clothes
questions.explanation: After using a washroom, you should wash your hands with soap and water to remove germs.
questions.misconception: Hand washing after using the washroom is not necessary.

questions.stem: What should you do with the toilet after using it?
questions.explanation: You should flush the toilet after using it to keep it clean.

questions.stem: Which of these is good washroom behaviour?
options: Flushing after use and washing hands
hints: Good behaviour keeps the washroom clean.
questions.explanation: Good washroom behaviour includes flushing after use and washing hands with soap and water.

questions.stem: Design a poster to encourage learners to keep the school washroom clean. Include at least two clear actions (e.g. 'Flush after use', 'Put tissue in the bin') and a short message.

criteria.description: Included at least two correct actions for keeping the washroom clean
Poster is neat and easy to understand

hints: Think about flushing and throwing tissue in the bin.
Write a short message like 'Keep our washroom clean!'
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.

questions.stem: Write a short message for a poster encouraging learners to keep the washroom clean.
answer: flush after use and wash your hands
let us keep the washroom clean
questions.explanation: A short message like 'Keep our washroom clean' encourages good habits.

questions.stem: List three rules you would put on a washroom poster to keep it clean.

criteria.description: Listed three clear and correct rules

hints: Think about flushing, tissue disposal, and hand washing.
questions.explanation: This is a written task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.

questions.stem: How can learners help keep school washrooms clean?
options: By flushing after use and putting tissue in the bin
By throwing tissue on the floor
hints: Good habits keep the washroom clean.
questions.explanation: Learners can help by flushing after use, putting tissue in the bin, and washing their hands.
questions.misconception: Learners cannot help keep washrooms clean.

questions.stem: State one way learners can help keep school washrooms clean.
answer: report dirty washrooms to the teacher
questions.explanation: Learners can help by flushing after use, putting tissue in the bin, and reporting problems to the teacher.
questions.misconception: Only adults can keep washrooms clean.

questions.stem: A learner notices that the school washroom is very dirty. What is the best action to take?
options: Tell the teacher so it can be cleaned
Close the washroom and never use it
hints: Tell an adult who can help.
questions.explanation: The best action is to tell the teacher so the washroom can be cleaned and kept healthy for everyone.
